profile.reading:
This is Facebook/Meta Altoona Data Center 3 on Meta's Altoona, Iowa campus. Meta broke ground on the Altoona campus in 2013 and has expanded it seven times since, most recently announced in December 2024, per Meta's own fact sheet and Data Center Frontier's reporting; Meta has invested more than $2.5 billion in the city of Altoona and the state of Iowa through this campus. Construction has employed an average of about 1,000 workers a year over twelve years, totaling 8.7 million work-hours, with peak skilled-trade staffing of 1,300 workers; day-to-day operations employ more than 400 people. Meta reports operational buildings on the campus are LEED Gold certified, that it matches all of its global electricity use with 100% clean and renewable energy, and that a Meta-supported project added 225 megawatts of new renewable generation capacity in Iowa. Meta says it has made more than 300 grants and sponsorships in the area since 2015 and provided more than $5.6 million in direct funding to Polk County-area schools and nonprofits. Meta does not publish a specific street address, building count, or per-building square footage for individual Altoona structures; the address above is derived from reverse-geocoding this building's mapped coordinates, not from an operator-published source, and should be treated as approximate.

Iowa has drawn more than $17 billion in data center capital investment, with 27 data centers operating or under construction statewide as of 2025, according to Inside Climate News; Microsoft, Google, Meta, and Apple together account for nearly all of that total. The state has led the nation in wind generation since adopting the first state renewable portfolio standard in 1983, with wind now supplying about 60% of Iowa's electricity and helping keep industrial power prices among the eighth-lowest in the country, both factors regional reporting ties directly to hyperscale operators' site selection in the Altoona/Des Moines corridor. That same reporting states Meta's Altoona campus has used up to 16% of the city of Altoona's water supply and consumed roughly 1.2 million megawatt-hours of electricity annually, and flags that federal cuts to clean-energy tax incentives under the 2025 One Big Beautiful Bill Act are projected by Energy Innovation to raise Iowa industrial electricity rates by 14 to 26 percent, a risk regional press has connected to the pace of further hyperscale investment in the state.

profile.capacity_note: Meta does not publish per-building IT capacity, square footage, or a building count for the Altoona campus; regional press (Data Center Frontier, citing Meta's own December 2024 announcement) reports the campus as a whole will exceed 5 million square feet on completion, expected in 2025, making it Meta's largest data center campus worldwide, surpassing Prineville, Oregon's 4.6 million square feet. No per-building figure is asserted here.

profile.regional_context: Altoona sits in the Des Moines metro area of central Iowa. Meta chose the site in part for MidAmerican Energy's wind-heavy generation mix and Iowa's wind-energy tax credits; MidAmerican has said it supplies its Iowa customers, Meta included, with wind generation matching 100% of retail load on an annual basis. Iowa's data center cluster in the Altoona/Des Moines area also includes Microsoft, Google, and Apple facilities, and the sector has become a significant driver of the state's industrial electricity demand and a subject of debate over local property-tax abatement policy, according to Inside Climate News and the Bend Bulletin-style local reporting seen in other Meta markets.

reading.body:
Meta's Altoona campus in Polk County is a multi-building hyperscale data center where the operator has invested $2.5 billion since breaking ground in 2013 and now employs over 400 operational staff. The campus specifications do not include published power capacity, total square footage, building count, or street address. Without a published megawatt figure, the campus cannot be ranked by IT load against other facilities, and the actual compute density it hosts remains unknown.

The campus achieves LEED Gold certification for operational buildings and operates on 100 percent renewable energy matched to its consumption. Meta is funding 225 megawatts of new renewable energy generation in Iowa as part of campus operations, though this state-level renewable capacity addition does not directly translate to the campus's own power draw or available headroom for scaling. Iowa has published power figures for only two data center facilities with a combined 18 megawatts of announced capacity, and this campus does not contribute to that total.

Without published power or floor space, this campus cannot be assessed for its role in current AI scaling constraints or grid binding capacity. Its scale relative to the 52 mapped facilities in Iowa, or its headroom for expansion, remains opaque from operator disclosures.
